sources.entry: beelzebub ⚠ - Honeypot framework designed to provide a highly secure environment for detecting and analyzing cyber attacks. (Source Code) MIT Docker/K8S/Go

summary.one_liner: Beelzebub is an open-source deception framework that runs configurable decoy services (SSH, HTTP, TCP, TELNET, MCP) to capture and log attacker interactions.
summary.what_it_does: Beelzebub lets you define decoy services and their response rules in YAML, then run them as a runtime that listens for attacker contact. Services can use static handlers for fixed responses or LLM-powered responses, which require a configured provider. Custom behavior can be added through trusted Go plugins compiled into the runtime. The framework records evidence such as commands, HTTP request details, and session context, depending on the protocol. Events can be inspected in local logs, published to RabbitMQ, or sent to the optional Beelzebub Platform. The README lists 18 example configurations covering remote access, web, databases, network services, IoT (MQTT), and MCP bait tools. Deployment options named are a local Go binary, Docker Compose, and Kubernetes with Helm.
use_cases: Detecting and analyzing attacks against decoy SSH or HTTP services
Simulating fake databases such as MySQL, Redis, or PostgreSQL as traps
Capturing prompt-injection attempts against AI agents using MCP bait tools
Monitoring decoy runtime activity with Prometheus metrics
Forwarding attacker interaction events to RabbitMQ
Running a lab honeypot with Docker Compose
how_to_run: curl -i <default HTTP decoy URL on port 8080>
notable: Decoy services defined declaratively in YAML, with static or LLM-powered responses
MCP bait tools for observing suspicious agent tool invocations
Trusted Go plugins compiled into the runtime via a public SDK
Structured event output to local logs, RabbitMQ, or the optional Beelzebub Platform
Prometheus metrics enabled via core.prometheus.enabled, disabled by default
caveats: Installer starts many example services including privileged ports; intended for an isolated lab host with authorization
On Linux the installer can enable host networking, which Docker does not isolate
LLM-based responses require a configured external provider
Go plugins execute in-process, so their source must be reviewed and versions pinned
